decisions.business: Visiting order of customers for each period and each vehicle; the distribution center is not written in the sequence but is implicit at the start and end of each non-empty route, so [1,3] means 0→1→3→0, and an empty list means the vehicle does not operate in that period.
decisions.shape: list[list[list[int]]], fixed outer shape [num_periods][num_vehicles][variable-length customer sequence]; customer numbers use 1,…,num_customers.
decisions.completeness: A list must be provided for every period and every vehicle slot, including empty lists for non-operating vehicles; within the same period each customer appears in at most one vehicle list, each non-empty list must not repeat customers, and must be consistent with the delivery records of the corresponding vehicle in deliveries.

decisions.business: Records, per period and per vehicle, the quantity of product delivered to each customer; this representation preserves the correspondence between delivery quantities and specific routes.
decisions.shape: list[list[list[float]]], fixed shape [num_periods][num_vehicles][num_customers]; deliveries[t][k][i-1] corresponds to period t+1, vehicle k+1, customer i.
decisions.completeness: All T×m×n values must be given and nonnegative; an entry must be 0 when the customer does not appear in the corresponding routes[t][k], the total delivery of each vehicle in each period must not exceed vehicle_capacity, and a customer may be served in a period only by the unique vehicle whose route contains it.

decisions.business: Gives the end-of-period inventory of the distribution center and all customers in each period after production, delivery, and demand are accounted for, used to verify inventory balance, stockouts, capacity, and holding costs.
decisions.shape: list[list[float]], fixed shape [num_periods][num_customers+1]; ending_inventories[t][0] is the distribution center inventory, ending_inventories[t][i] is the inventory of customer i.
decisions.completeness: The distribution center and all customer inventories must be given for every period and must strictly satisfy inventory balance with the initial inventories, production, demand, and deliveries; all end-of-period inventories must be nonnegative, the distribution center end-of-period inventory must not exceed its capacity, and a customer's inventory after receiving goods and before demand occurs must not exceed its capacity.
